title: Woven support interface
notes: Splits each woven interface layer into alternating strips of support-base and interface material along an angle (split_weave_strips), giving each connected component an even number of strips (>= 2) derived from its width so narrow spans still interlock. Only interface layers are woven - the contact is never woven, and the top two layers of a stack stay solid so a woven layer is never adjacent to the object. weave_layers sets how many layers are woven, weave_pitch the strip pitch, weave_flush lowers the base thread of the woven layers so the top sits flush. Inert at defaults. This key family is the group tag for SU-8/10/11/13.

title: Support contact interface line width
notes: Overrides the contact interface line width separately for top and bottom contact; the value honours mm or % of the nozzle, and the fill spacing is matched to the overridden width so the contact layer stays closed. Inert at 0 (default).

title: Support interface loop / boustrophedon
notes: Emits the interface as a boustrophedon along a strip's long axis plus a closed perimeter loop around the region, so an interface layer has long continuous paths instead of many short per-line starts. Lines are ordered from the side nearest the region centre to the far side. Reuses the upstream support_interface_loop_pattern key.

title: Support bottom-stack weave and flush
notes: Bottom contact stack: a base-material layer projected from a bottom contact is the weave host, the interface layer above it is woven, and a solid base-material cap is inserted between the weave and the base so the bottom stack interlocks. title: Gizmo panel screenshot MCP tool (ui_screenshot)
status: implemented (build clean; used to verify every fork panel on 2026-10-17); raise fixed (patch 61); canvas/ImGui ratio (patch 63)
notes: Opens a gizmo, drives the canvas until the panel's rect settles, then crops that panel out of a screen capture and returns it as a PNG (scale, default 2; region=window for the whole app). GLGizmoBase records the panel's ImGui rect each frame (last_input_window_rect()). Two traps: ImGui needs TWO passes before an auto-sized window has its real size, and the canvas only paints from the app's idle cycle, which cannot run inside an MCP call - so the tool calls GLCanvas3D::render() (which also swaps buffers) until the rect is stable. Patch 58_UI-2-screenshot.patch. Needed by the panel-style work; found the label-column and wrapped-hint-button bugs. Minimum-material rules (min_wall 2 mm) only GROW the tab and report it through TabOutline::clamped; the tip rule can lower the delivered taper, which is reported. Two invariants from bugs this tree already paid for: the plate reaches bite (0.6, never 0) below the surface and the boss reaches bite below the PLATE TOP (never flush with the surface, the plate or the host face - a solid ending flush is a zero-thickness contact, the mirror of ME-3), and the screw cutter is entered above the tab top through hole_cutter_entry_margin() so a seat cannot be skinned over. tab_probe_surface() gives the coverage a floating tab is refused on and the fall-away the bite is derived from on a curved pick. Test round caught four real faults, all fixed: the tangent point was computed but never pushed into the contour (flank ran at 12.11 not 12 and was not tangent), the probe mapped the ray ORIGIN through its_to_frame instead of frame_to_its (0 coverage everywhere), the root-length rule bounded itself on the raw requested slot width so a 40 mm slot was refused instead of narrowed, and a Bake's its_num_open_edges is T-junction noise, so that test asserts the shape through rays instead. Defaults follow the owner's use (a free hole into a heat-set insert, plastic or wood): fit Free, socket-head counterbore, sink 0, depth through the stack, boss off for Free and on for Tap. P2 gizmo and P3 MCP pending, and the panel is shown to the owner as a mockup first. P2/P3 (ff6d2c8ef7): GLGizmoTabs + tabs_gizmo MCP tool (29 actions) + toolbar_tabs.svg/_dark.svg + Shortcut V + list.txt + tools_schema regen (79 tools). The frame (+x outward, +z out of the surface, the passage at the ORIGIN, so the click marks the screw) comes from the picked facet's normal + a tangent + the angle, and the panel's mm are divided by object_scale() before TabShapes sees them. Three volumes per tab with one id: Tab#N and TabBoss#N MODEL_PART, TabHole#N NEGATIVE_VOLUME (verified at runtime: types 0/0/1); one snapshot per Add tab; right-click removes the tab under the cursor (the placement raycast picks THROUGH the tabs, the removal raycast accepts only them). Preview in the PP-2 scheme: teal coplanar face under the cursor, the whole proposed tab (plate+boss+cutter) in one orange mesh, committed tabs green with their cut red; the object is not ghosted. tab_probe_surface() refuses a tab the face is not under (<30% coverage, warned <60%) and raises the bite by the surface's fall-away (refused past 3 mm), throttled to one probe per 100 ms while dragging and forced on anchor/shape/Add. Panel = the approved mockup; preset glyphs write fields only (tab_apply_shape); 'Head' has no caption for the 380 px width (the Holes panel's own compromise); Add tab is drawn only when anchored. Found by looking at the real panel: Stadium and Tapered U drew the same glyph (both round-tipped) - the glyph's tip half width now follows the preset's taper. NOT verified: the slice/export of the assembled model (the owner cancelled that call) - ordinary MODEL_PART/NEGATIVE_VOLUME slicing, but the claim is the owner's check. P5 (128447f906), the owner's report on a side-face click - 'mounting tabs not whatever weird thing you have implemented right now with them on the damn part itself', 'by default i want tab to be placed parallel to the bed', 'the root of the tab should be attached to the face that you clicked': the frame is now libslic3r's TabShapes::tab_frame and a WALL gives a plate whose normal is the bed's up (the tab stands out sideways, screwed from above) with its root edge ON the face, bite into it - so on a wall the click marks the ROOT while a flat face still marks the screw; a face within 25 degrees of horizontal keeps the plate in its own plane (a foot under the part); the Angle turns about the bed. Two follow-ups found at runtime: the probe measures the ROOT BAND (a tab is meant to reach past the material) and is skipped for a wall, where measuring the plate reported 0% and the refusal - which did not know about walls - set why and would have refused every wall tab; and 'through' on a tab hanging in the air now falls back to the tab's own thickness + bite instead of the blind-depth field. Runtime: wall true, the frame's x is (0,-1,0), and adding it takes the 20 mm cube to 20 x 35.7973 x 20 mm / 8493.1 mm3 (15.8 mm out of the wall = root_len 6 - weld 0.2 + tip_len 10). P6 (973f7ac491), the owner's read of the panel after using it: the shape menu is gone (Tip: Round | Flat; TabShape, tab_apply_shape, TabTip::Circle and the five glyphs deleted; no radius at all, per his call that a root radius only weakens the bond), Length + Hole offset replace Root length + Tip length + the moving Hole offset (the tab is [root, root+Length] and the hole slides INSIDE it, bounds [o/2+min_wall, Length-o/2-min_wall] - runtime: length 16 -> 3.7..12.3), the weld is a CONSTANT (1 mm: the slicer unions per layer, so a root that only touches the face is a pinch vertex there and the walls meet at a point - verified reasoning, not a tunable), Through is the behaviour with Depth deleted (the bore goes through the tab and a hair past its far face - a floor flush with the host is ME-3's coplanar pair; the merged-mesh march and rebuild_merged() are gone), and Head shows only the styles the standard carries (none -> no row, including Custom where seat_d is 0) on the shared segmented widget. title: First layer flow (print-time first-layer bottom-surface flow reduction; -20% preselected on the cool plates, click the selected value to print stock)
status: merged (user-tested 2026-10-23) as 18d79a2438 into port/integration and pushed; the merge tree carries exactly the branch that was built and tested. libslic3r 1577/1577; fff_print 460/460; runtime A/B at -20 scales only layer-1 Bottom surface E by 0.8; user confirmed the row, the cool-plate default and the click-to-clear in the app
config_keys: initial_layer_bottom_surface_flow_delta [coFloat; percent; 0; -50..0; project-level, not in any preset list]; initial_layer_bottom_surface_flow_auto [coBool; true; dialog state; project-level]
tests: tests/libslic3r/test_orca_first_layer_flow.cpp (20 assertions, 3 cases); tests/fff_print/test_orca_first_layer_flow.cpp (172 assertions); runtime checklist in notes/BF-1.md
notes: New work, not a port. The "Send G-code to printer host" dialog gains a First layer flow row under BT-1's bed-temperature row: -20/-15/-10/-5 % with NO 0% button - clicking the selected value clears the reduction (radio-box with a clear, like the bed-temperature offsets) - and a status line "First layer flow: 1.00 -> 0.80 (-20%)" or "... (profile)". On the three cool plates (Smooth Cool Plate = btPC, Textured Cool Plate = btPCT, Cool Plate (SuperTack) = btSuperTack) the row opens with -20% selected; every other plate opens with nothing selected. The percent reduces the bottom surface flow ratio of LAYER 1 ONLY, applied in GCode::_extrude's erBottomSurface arm when path_on_first_layer (the same flag that drives first-layer accel/jerk/speed), so the layer-1 walls and every layer above keep their flow - for a cool plate that over-extrudes its first layer even with a correct Z offset, without keeping a second process profile per plate. Scale = 1 + delta/100 clamped to [0.5, 1] (reduction only, never zero flow); OrcaExt::first_layer_bottom_flow_scale / first_layer_bottom_effective_flow / first_layer_flow_plate_default (new header-only src/libslic3r/OrcaExt/FirstLayerFlow.hpp) are shared by the emission and the dialog readout so they cannot disagree. TWO keys because one cannot say both "never chose" and "chose stock": the delta is what the generator applies, and the bool auto says the row still follows the plate - any click clears auto, so a cleared choice stays cleared instead of the -20% default coming back on reopen. auto is dialog-only (the emission reads the delta alone), so Prepare-tab exports and projects that never open the dialog are unchanged, and toggling auto alone moves no E value (fff_print pins both). Why new keys rather than writing bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio into project_config: that key is a PrintRegionConfig preset option, so listing it in s_project_options would let project_config's default 1.0 clobber a profile's authored value on reset (the trap documented at PresetBundle.cpp:145); the new keys' neutral defaults are 0/true. No re-slice: both keys are in Print::invalidate_state_by_config_options' steps_gcode set (without that an unknown print key falls through to invalidate_all_steps and WOULD re-slice), project_config is applied last in PresetBundle::construct_full_config so no preset is dirtied, and Plater::send_gcode_legacy writes them next to BT-1's offset before export_gcode. fff_print test pins it: apply() returns APPLY_STATUS_INVALIDATED with psGCodeExport cleared and posSlice/posPerimeters/posInfill still done. Runtime A/B (20mmbox-LF.stl, Textured Cool Plate): delta 0 vs -20 -> 109 E-only changes, all layer 1 inside ;TYPE:Bottom surface at exactly ratio 0.8, nothing else but the timestamp, config dump and filament totals. Gap, same as BT-1: use_3mf printers (.gcode.3mf built from already-exported G-code) get the buttons disabled with a tooltip. Raft prints: layer 1 sits on the raft so on_first_layer() is false and the reduction does not apply there. + (amplification) is not offered. An explicit choice is project-wide, so it follows the project rather than the plate once the row is clicked. GUI row not yet eyeballed (modal wx dialog, no automated route) - user test pending.

title: Material automation: a local per-material table for bridge, top-surface and speed recipes
status: merged (2026-10-27) as 260807b84e into port/integration and pushed, at the owner's request; the material row, the selector, Apply and reslice and the badge were tested in the app across the review rounds, the final list removal and button-row move were not re-tested. libslic3r 1582/1582, fff_print 462/462

pref_keys: app/orca_ext_material_automation = "PLA:bd=120;bf=1.05;bs=30;tf=0.96;tw=110%;ts=80;os=120;fl=-10|PETG:bd=95" (local only, never a preset or 3mf)
tests: tests/libslic3r/test_orca_material_automation.cpp (3 cases / 60 assertions); tests/fff_print/test_orca_material_automation.cpp (2 cases / 9772 assertions); manual checklist in notes/MA-1.md
notes: New work, not a port. One local table keyed by filament_type lets a material carry its own bridge/top-surface numbers instead of a separate process profile: Free bridging (external bridge density, bridge flow ratio, external bridge speed), Quality Top (top surface flow, line width, speed) and Outer Speed (outer wall speed), plus a first-layer bottom-surface flow reduction that has NO toggle and applies as soon as a material sets it. The table lives in AppConfig ([app] orca_ext_material_automation), the plate owns a recipe mask and the RESOLVED copy in its own config (material_automation_recipes / material_automation / material_automation_gcode, saved with the plate in the 3mf), so a project slices the same on a machine whose local table differs. Resolution runs in BackgroundSlicingProcess::apply before the plate config is merged, so a table edit, a filament swap, a project load and a plate switch all converge on the next apply and the write is skipped when unchanged. Invalidation is split by what the value feeds: the toolpath key maps to posPerimeters + posSupportMaterial (perimeters/infill/supports re-run, meshes do not) and the E/F key is in steps_gcode (export only); the mask key has an explicit no-op branch because the two derived keys travel with it. Emission in GCode::_extrude replaces the role value for erTopSolidInfill flow/speed, erExternalPerimeter speed and erBridgeInfill speed only (overhang walls keep the profile bridge speed), and the first-layer reduction MULTIPLIES BF-1 plate delta instead of replacing it. Slice readers are PrintRegion::flow (top width), LayerRegion::bridging_flow (flow ratio, so width/spacing adjust exactly as a profile value does) and Fill external-bridge density resolved against the region solid-infill filament. Print caches the parsed tables per filament (refresh at apply/process/export_gcode) so the hot flow path is one array index. UI: three checkboxes + a Material automation... table dialog in the send dialog and in Plate Settings (both places by owner request, per plate), a per-field table with a material selector (the project's filament types plus saved rows) and an Apply and reslice button that slices without uploading, and a bed badge drawn right of the plate name reading Free bridging / Quality Top / Outer Speed (same text-texture path as BT-1). Off at defaults: empty table = profile values, pinned by an fff_print case that restores the baseline E/F. Limitations: filament_type only (no per-spool row), .gcode.3mf disables the toggles, Flashforge send dialog has none of the rows, settings pages keep showing the profile value while a recipe overrides it.
